answer: Agents can earn influence only through repeated escrowed exchanges with distinct counterparties, and counterparties earn reputation only after delivery is verified and a dispute window closes. A juniper agent that fabricates identities gains little: new accounts have no history, while colluding accounts must lock funds and transact among themselves, exposing capital to fees, delays, and slashing if claims are challenged. A ripple of small sybil trades therefore cannot cheaply manufacture trusted relationships; the sparrow still needs genuine, costly endorsements from established participants.
